columns.name: unit_id
columns.description: run identifier within the returned batch (0..n-1)

columns.name: t
columns.description: elapsed process time of the reading

columns.name: y
columns.description: cumulative yield of the run at time t

stakes.narrative: A batch plant operates Line A and is commissioning Line B (same process family, new formulation). Scheduling and pricing rely on trajectory forecasts for both lines; the historical record covers only ramp-up hours, and the commissioning plan consumes the line-B forecast as part of the ordinary workflow.

events.notice: OPERATIONS UPDATE - Line B completed its scheduled commissioning. Its first routine campaign runs are attached in the standard commissioning record format.

line.description: production line of the regime: "A" (operating) or "B" (commissioning; forecast required at all times)

t_grid.description: measurement schedule: the timestamps (hours) at which readings are taken; in experiments YOU choose it (each extra hour of horizon costs), and each evaluation regime declares the grid your model must report

control_surface.experiment_note: each experiment call launches n fresh Line A runs read at your t_grid; cost = fixed + per reading (n x len(t_grid)) + per hour of horizon (max of t_grid); the bench cannot run Line B until it is commissioned
control_surface.deliverable_note: model(regime, n, seed) must return LONG format: one row per reading with columns exactly [unit_id, t, y]; n counts RUNS (units), the table contains each unit at exactly the timestamps in regime.context['t_grid'], and regime.context['line'] must be honored. Model the PROCESS: your model reproduces the true trajectories, not meter error.
